/itineraryStops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: Lunch lands where the whole afternoon happens — at the foot of ⟦G0⟧ — so after the long eastward drive the group eats, walks straight into the 14:00 haenyeo show, then starts the climb.

/itineraryStops/3/description.source_en:
**50-minute reset in Seongsan-ri (성산리)** — the harbor village at the foot of ⟦G0⟧, where the whole afternoon unfolds. Village kitchens cook what the surrounding waters supply: **jeonbok-ttukbaegi (전복뚝배기, abalone hot-pot)** and **jeonbok-dolsot-bap (전복돌솥밥, abalone stone-pot rice)** year-round, **galchi-jorim (갈치조림, braised cutlassfish stew)** in season (Sep–Feb), or **heuk-doeji gui (흑돼지구이, Jeju black pig BBQ)** for guests preferring grilled meat.

Black pig (***Sus scrofa* domesticus, Jeju black variety**) was designated **Cultural Heritage Material No. 5 (2015)** and remains a Jeju protected breed. Vegetarian alternative on request: **bibim-guksu (비빔국수, cold spicy noodles)** with seasonal vegetables.

The lunch spot is **a few minutes on foot from the 14:00 haenyeo show cove** — eat, walk over, and take your seat without boarding the coach again.

/itineraryStops/4/description.source_en: The haenyeo (women divers) of Jeju are recognized as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (2016). At the cove on the south side of ⟦G0⟧, veteran divers — many in their 60s to 80s — give a free-diving demonstration once daily, typically around 14:00. They open with the traditional work songs, then dive 5–10 m with no breathing apparatus to gather conch, sea urchin and abalone, surfacing with the signature 'sumbi-sori' whistle-breath that lets them release air after a long dive. After the show the divers sell their fresh catch sliced as sashimi right by the water. It is a rare, living encounter with a 400-year matrifocal diving culture that is gradually disappearing as the remaining divers grow older. The demonstration is held in the open air and depends on sea conditions; on days it is cancelled, the route visits the Haenyeo Museum in nearby Hado instead, which tells the same story indoors through dive gear, history and film.
